evidence: The survivor uses "backtracking for independent set" and represents conflicts with "adj = [0] * n" and bit masks.
affordance_in_statement: The system architecture guarantees that collisions are strictly pairwise; ... a payload is considered stable if and only if no two modules selected for the payload form one of the m identified colliding pairs.
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving removal: this pairwise non-collision condition is exactly the independent-set task. Removing or weakening it would change the problem rather than merely re-present it.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Directly models the instance as a graph and searches for an independent set using bitmask backtracking.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: A stable payload is defined solely by the absence of colliding pairs among its selected modules.

common_affordance: The stable-payload condition is exactly the existence of an independent set of size k in a graph of pairwise collisions.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its generic bitmask backtracking search for an independent set is exponential and timed out on hard instances.
It enumerates every k-subset with itertools.combinations, which is prohibitively exponential for n up to 46.
Its minimum-degree greedy selection is not a correct algorithm for maximum or exact-size independent set and can miss a valid payload.

recommended_edit: No single semantics-preserving edit can defeat the survivor: the shared affordance is the core computational task. Doing so would require changing the collision model, adding a restrictive graph-class promise, or changing the task itself.
